name: Beagle 2
lastSignal: No confirmed signal after expected landing on December 25, 2003
tagline: It appears to have reached Mars. What never arrived was the message saying it had made it.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Search for evidence of life and study the geology and environment of Mars as part of the European Mars Express mission.
beats.achieved: Beagle 2 separated from Mars Express and apparently reached the Martian surface on Christmas Day 2003. Later orbital images showed the lander at its planned landing region.
beats.ending: No signal was received after landing. Images taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and released in 2015 showed Beagle 2 on the surface with some of its solar panels apparently deployed, suggesting that the deployment sequence had not completed.
beats.now: The lander remains at Isidis Planitia on Mars. It is not operational, and its precise internal failure sequence is not fully known.
beats.learned: The mission highlighted the difficulty of entry, descent and landing on Mars and the importance of designing robust communication and deployment systems.
